\chapter{Graph Theory — Optimality}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.GraphTheory.Kruskal.Optimality
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This chapter establishes the correctness and optimality of Kruskal's algorithm on a
weighted edge list over the vertex set $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$: the greedy loop
$\texttt{Kruskal.processEdges}$ preserves the connectivity partition of its input, and the
resulting edge set $\texttt{Kruskal.kruskal}$ spans exactly what the input spans while
having minimum total weight among all spanning subsets of the input.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Union--find state after the greedy loop]
\lean{Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges}
\label{Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.UF, Kruskal.UF.find, Kruskal.UF.merge, Kruskal.WEdge}
The union--find structure obtained by running the greedy loop over a list of weighted
edges: starting from a state $uf$, each edge $e$ is merged into the state when its
endpoints $e.u$ and $e.v$ currently lie in different components, and is ignored
otherwise. Unlike $\texttt{Kruskal.processEdges}$ it returns only the final state, not the
list of accepted edges.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Greedy loop and unconditional merge give the same partition]
\lean{Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges_partition}
\label{Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges_partition}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.UF, Kruskal.UF.SamePartition, Kruskal.UF.merge, Kruskal.UF.mergeAll, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.merge_noop, Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges}
\difficulty{4}
Fix $n \in \bbn$, let $\mathit{es}$ be a list of weighted edges over $n$ vertices, and
let $\mathit{uf} : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbn$ be an initial union--find state. The greedy
loop, which scans $\mathit{es}$ in order and merges the endpoints of each edge only when
they currently carry different representatives, yields a final state that induces the
same partition of the vertices as the unconditional fold, which merges the endpoints of
every edge of $\mathit{es}$ in order without regard to their current components. That
is, for all $i, j : \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, nodes $i$ and $j$ share a representative in the
greedy-loop state if and only if they share a representative in the unconditional-fold
state.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Accumulator splits off as a reversed prefix]
\lean{Kruskal.processEdges_acc}
\label{Kruskal.processEdges_acc}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.UF, Kruskal.UF.merge, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.processEdges}
\difficulty{4}
Fix $n \in \bbn$, and let $\mathit{es}$ be a list of weighted edges over $n$ vertices,
$\mathit{uf}$ a union-find state on $n$ nodes, and $\mathit{acc}$ a list of weighted
edges over $n$ vertices. Then running the edge-selection sweep on $\mathit{es}$ from
state $\mathit{uf}$ with initial accumulator $\mathit{acc}$ yields the reversal of
$\mathit{acc}$ concatenated (on the left) with the result of running the same sweep on
$\mathit{es}$ from the same state $\mathit{uf}$ but with the empty accumulator.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Edge selection preserves the induced partition]
\lean{Kruskal.processEdges_same_partition}
\label{Kruskal.processEdges_same_partition}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.UF, Kruskal.UF.SamePartition, Kruskal.UF.find, Kruskal.UF.mergeAll, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.processEdges, Kruskal.processEdges_acc, Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges, Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges_partition}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n \in \bbn$, let $\mathit{uf} : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbn$ be a union-find state,
and let $\mathit{es}$ be a list of weighted edges over $n$ vertices. Merging into
$\mathit{uf}$ only the edges retained by the edge-selection sweep (running the sweep
from $\mathit{uf}$ with an empty accumulator) yields a union-find state inducing the
same equivalence relation on nodes as merging all of $\mathit{es}$ into $\mathit{uf}$:
for all $i, j : \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, the two nodes share a representative after the first
process exactly when they share a representative after the second.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Skipping an intra-component edge in the sweep]
\lean{Kruskal.processEdges_skip}
\label{Kruskal.processEdges_skip}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.UF, Kruskal.UF.find, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.processEdges}
\difficulty{1}
Fix a number of nodes $n$, a union-find state $\mathit{uf} : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbn$,
a weighted edge $e$ over $n$ vertices with endpoints $u$ and $v$, and a list
$\mathit{rest}$ of further weighted edges over $n$ vertices. Suppose the two endpoints
of $e$ already have the same representative in $\mathit{uf}$, that is, $\mathit{uf}(u) =
\mathit{uf}(v)$. Then the edge-selection sweep applied to the list $e :: \mathit{rest}$
starting from state $\mathit{uf}$ with empty accumulator returns exactly the same edge
list as the sweep applied to $\mathit{rest}$ starting from the same state $\mathit{uf}$
with empty accumulator.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Weight contributed by an accepted edge]
\lean{Kruskal.processEdges_take_weight}
\label{Kruskal.processEdges_take_weight}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.UF, Kruskal.UF.find, Kruskal.UF.merge, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.processEdges, Kruskal.processEdges_acc, Kruskal.totalWeight}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a natural number $n$ and a union-find state $\mathit{uf}$ over $n$ nodes, and let
$e$ be a weighted edge over $n$ vertices — with endpoints $u_e, v_e$ and weight $w_e$ —
followed by a list $\mathit{rest}$ of further weighted edges. Suppose the endpoints of
$e$ lie in different components, that is, $\mathit{uf}(u_e) \ne \mathit{uf}(v_e)$. Then
the total weight of the edge-selection sweep applied to the list $e :: \mathit{rest}$
starting from $\mathit{uf}$ and an empty accumulator equals $w_e$ plus the total weight
of the sweep applied to $\mathit{rest}$ starting from an empty accumulator and the state
obtained by merging the components of $u_e$ and $v_e$ in $\mathit{uf}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Optimality of the greedy edge-selection sweep]
\lean{Kruskal.processEdges_optimal}
\label{Kruskal.processEdges_optimal}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.Reach, Kruskal.UF, Kruskal.UF.SamePartition, Kruskal.UF.SamePartition.symm, Kruskal.UF.SamePartition.trans, Kruskal.UF.find, Kruskal.UF.merge, Kruskal.UF.mergeAll, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.erase_append_perm, Kruskal.mergeAll_cons_eq, Kruskal.mergeAll_iff_reach, Kruskal.mergeAll_perm, Kruskal.merge_noop, Kruskal.processEdges, Kruskal.processEdges_skip, Kruskal.processEdges_take_weight, Kruskal.reduce_to_rest, Kruskal.totalWeight, Kruskal.totalWeight_erase, Kruskal.uf_exchange}
\difficulty{6}
Let $\mathit{edges}$ be a list of weighted edges on $n$ vertices, sorted in
nondecreasing order of weight, and let $\mathit{uf}$ be a union-find state whose induced
partition is exactly the reachability relation of some base edge list $\mathit{base}$:
for all vertices $a$ and $b$, the representatives $\mathit{uf}(a)$ and $\mathit{uf}(b)$
are equal if and only if $a$ and $b$ are joined by a path through the edges of
$\mathit{base}$. Let $S$ be any list of edges, each of which occurs in $\mathit{edges}$,
such that merging all of $S$ into $\mathit{uf}$ and merging all of $\mathit{edges}$ into
$\mathit{uf}$ yield the same partition of the vertices. Then the greedy sweep — which
starts from $\mathit{uf}$, scans $\mathit{edges}$ in order, and keeps each edge exactly
when its two endpoints lie in currently distinct components — produces a set of edges
whose total weight is at most the total weight of $S$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Kruskal's output preserves connectivity]
\lean{Kruskal.kruskal_spans}
\label{Kruskal.kruskal_spans}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.Reach, Kruskal.SpansLike, Kruskal.UF.init, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.kruskal, Kruskal.mergeAll_init_iff, Kruskal.processEdges_same_partition, Kruskal.reach_mono}
\difficulty{3}
Fix $n \in \bbn$, and let $E$ be a list of weighted edges on the vertex set
$\mathrm{Fin}\,n$. Then the edge list $\mathrm{kruskal}\,n\,E$ produced by Kruskal's
algorithm on $E$ spans $E$: for every pair of vertices $u, v \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, if
$u$ and $v$ are connected by a path through the edges of $E$, then they are also
connected by a path through the selected edges $\mathrm{kruskal}\,n\,E$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Optimality of Kruskal's algorithm]
\lean{Kruskal.kruskal_optimal}
\label{Kruskal.kruskal_optimal}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.SpansLike, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.kruskal, Kruskal.mergeAll_init_iff, Kruskal.processEdges_optimal, Kruskal.reach_mono, Kruskal.totalWeight}
\difficulty{5}
Let $E$ be a list of weighted edges on $n$ vertices, and let $S$ be another such list in
which every edge is also an edge of $E$. Suppose that $S$ spans like $E$: whenever two
vertices $u$ and $v$ are joined by a path through the edges of $E$, they are also joined
by a path through the edges of $S$. Let $K$ denote the edge list produced by Kruskal's
algorithm on $E$, and write $w(e)$ for the weight of an edge $e$. Then the total weight
of $K$ is no greater than that of $S$:
\[
  \sum_{e \in K} w(e) \;\le\; \sum_{e \in S} w(e).
\]
\end{theorem}
